To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

13C-labled pyruvate affors selective labeling at C1′ and C5′ positions of ribose ring, and C2, C5, and C8 of purine bases and C5 of pyrimidine bases, with minimal labeling elsewhere in the ribonucleotid.

1) the use of 13C asymmetrically labeled pyruvate as a carbon source for E. coli affords site specific labeling of the ribose and purine and pyrimidine bases in nucleotides; 2) this labeling pattern is superior to those achieved with [1,3-13C] glycerol for NMR spectroscopic studies of RNA structure and dynamics; 3) this approach is readily scalable to larger RNAs.
13C-labelling of the RNA backbone and nucleobase of the 30S rRNA is feasible using a pyruvate-based labelling strategy.
In summary, our research is concerned with
developing new labeling strategies that can be used to probe the structure and dynamics in RNA using NMR spectroscopy and to understand the role of RNA in biological processes.
the development of new labeling strategies for RNA that are compatible with high resolution NMR studies.
the development and implementation of new labeling strategies for NMR studies of RNA.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the use of [3-13 C]-pyruvated DL323 E. Coli is the best way of labeling RNA for NMR studies.
the labeling patterns obtained with DL323 and 13C-pyruvates are superior to the commonly used labeling patterns obtained with 13C-glycerol.
this is an important advance in NMR spectroscopy of RNA.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that

the use of 3-pyrvuic acid as a precursor for RNA labeling in bacteria provides a unique opportunity to selectively label the RNA backbone and the base moieties, which can greatly simplify NMR spectra and facilitate the study of the dynamics of RNA by NMR.

the use of [3-13c]-pyruvates as the sole carbon source for DL323 strains leads to selective labeling of the ribose C5′ and C1′, purine C8 and C2 and pyrimidine positions C5 and C6, which are not available with the use of [1, 13c]-glycerol as the sole carbon sources.
the use of asymmetric 13C-labelling in the ribose moiety provides a significant improvement over the use of uniformly labelled nucleotides for structural and dynamics studies of nucleic acid systems.
The main takeaway from our work is that

13C labeled pyruvate is a useful carbon source for selective isotopic labeling of RNA and the labeling pattern is highly dependent on the carbon source and the genetic background of the E. coli strain.
13C-labelling with [3-13c] pyruvate is a very powerful method to selectively label RNA for NMR studies.
13C-labelling of nucleotides with [3-13 C]-pyruvates is an effective way to label RNA and is superior to the use of [1, 13 C]-glycerol.
